title: SAIPH neural networks predict future suicidal ideation risk from Twitter data
summary: Neural networks trained on psychological constructs in tweets fed a random forest that predicted suicidal ideation status; on an independent set of 277 ideators the AUC was 0.88. Individual risk peaks marked about a 7-fold increased risk of ideation in the following 10 days (OR 6.7), and scores were associated with county-wide suicide death rates.
ai_technology: Neural networks and random forest on Twitter text (SAIPH)
organization: University of Ottawa (The Royal's Institute of Mental Health Research)

evidence.tested: Independent set of 277 suicidal ideators and regional Twitter data compared with county suicide death rates.
evidence.unknown: Social-media proxy for ideation; county-level validation is ecological; not a validated clinical tool; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks scored tweets for suicide-related constructs and a random forest predicted ideation risk.
